title: ‘Chrysalis’ Lands Vietnam Theatrical Deal With CJ CGV, Sets September Release (EXCLUSIVE)
description: “Chrysalis” has secured a theatrical distribution deal in Vietnam through CJ CGV Vietnam, the country’s leading multiplex operator and distributor,
body:
“Chrysalis” has secured a theatrical distribution deal in Vietnam through CJ CGV Vietnam, the country’s leading multiplex operator and distributor, with a nationwide release set for Sept. 11. 

	The film will open locally as “Mãi Nợ Một Lời Tạm Biệt,” rendered in English as “The Farewell I Never Gave.” The international title remains “Chrysalis.”

	The deal marks a significant distribution milestone for the U.S.-Vietnam production, which is set in Vietnam and draws on the childhood memories of its subject and executive producer, Sir Daniel K. Winn. “Bringing ‘Chrysalis’ to theaters in Vietnam is deeply personal,” Winn said. “This story grew out of my childhood and the love of my grandmother, and I hope Vietnamese audiences see something of their own families and memories in it.”
	

	Directed by J. Robert Schulz from a screenplay by Andrew Creme, based on a story by Winn, Randall J. Slavin and Schulz, the film stars Kieu Chinh as Bà Nội, the grandmother at the heart of the story, with Winn appearing in the present-day storyline. The cast also includes Uy Nhan, Samuel An, Lan Thy, Le Anh Huy, Tien Pham and Trinh Tu Trung. WS Productions produced.


	“This Vietnam release is an important milestone for ‘Chrysalis’ and reflects the collaboration between our U.S. and Vietnamese cast, crew and producing teams,” executive producer Slavin said. “We are proud to bring the film to audiences in the country where its story begins.”

	The film made its market debut at the 2026 Cannes Film Market with two market screenings before going on to compete at the fourth edition of the Danang Asian Film Festival, where it was one of 13 films selected for the Asian Competition. At DANAFF, Kieu Chinh received the Screen Excellence Merit Award, recognizing a screen career spanning nearly seven decades and more than 100 roles.
	

	“‘Chrysalis’ is a deeply moving story that explores the powerful themes of family and memory,” CJ CGV Vietnam said in a statement. “We look forward to bringing this remarkable award-winning film to audiences across Vietnam this September.”

	The Vietnam theatrical run is part of the film’s broader release schedule, which includes a Beverly Hills engagement in October and a worldwide rollout planned for November.

title: Immersive Cinematic Art Platform Xinemarte Makes Malaysia Debut at MIFFest With ‘The Room Remembers’
description: Xinemarte, the immersive cinematic art platform developed by Los Angeles-based creative technology company SQNXR, has made its Malaysia premiere as
body:
Xinemarte, the immersive cinematic art platform developed by Los Angeles-based creative technology company SQNXR, has made its Malaysia premiere as a special program at the recently concluded 9th Malaysia International Film Festival in Kuala Lumpur.

	The platform’s Kuala Lumpur rollout began a day ahead of MIFFest‘s opening, and marks the second stop in Xinemarte’s Asian expansion following a soft launch in Taipei.


	The Malaysia program centers on “The Room Remembers,” Xinemarte’s inaugural thematic chapter, and its first presentation, “Fluid” – a 25-minute audiovisual work by SQNXR Creative Director Ray Tijssen, who operates under the alias 0010×0010. The work treats the movie theater itself as the primary artistic medium, drawing on cinematic-scale projection and Dolby Atmos surround sound to create a shared sensory environment.
	

	“You have canvas, you have screens, you have sculpture and you have movie theatre rooms,” Tijssen said. “The room becomes the audience. The room remembers.”

	Tijssen described “Fluid” as “organic forms adrift in a single current, where solid and liquid move as one, somewhere between deep ocean and deep space.”

	MIFFest audiences attended a special post-screening Q&A session with Tijssen, in which he discussed the creative process behind the work and the concept underpinning “The Room Remembers.” The screenings drew a positive response from festival-goers, with many describing the experience as calming and meditative.

	Jazzy Group of Companies, the Malaysia-based entertainment company and MIFFest organizer, holds the exclusive Asia sales mandate for Xinemarte. CEO Joanne Goh founded the festival.
	

	“Cinema infrastructure is underutilized for significant portions of the day,” Goh said. “Xinemarte allows operators to activate those spaces with premium experiential content that appeals to audiences who might never attend a traditional film screening. We see enormous potential across the region.”

	Structured around 25-minute cycles with staggered start times, the platform allows audiences to enter and exit freely, with programming updated monthly across family-friendly and adult-oriented categories. Rather than adapting conventional content for cinema screens, Xinemarte was built to exploit the full capabilities of contemporary theatrical infrastructure.

	Following its Malaysia run, the platform is set to expand to Singapore, Hong Kong and additional markets across the region. Tijssen, who was born in the Netherlands and is now based in Los Angeles, has previously mounted installations at MOCA Bangkok, W1 London and TODA Dubai.

schema.headline: Immersive Cinematic Art Platform Xinemarte Makes Malaysia Debut at MIFFest With ‘The Room Remembers’

title: Ariana Grande Sues Hackers for Leaking Unreleased Music and Footage
description: Ariana Grande has filed a lawsuit against anonymous hackers, claiming that they gained backdoor access to devices that led to the leak of unreleased
body:
Ariana Grande has filed a lawsuit against anonymous hackers, claiming that they gained backdoor access to devices that led to the leak of unreleased songs and footage from recording sessions and music videos.

	The suit, filed on Monday in Los Angeles and reviewed by Variety, targets a group of unnamed John Does for phishing scams and hacking schemes that have caused “unlawful and egregious theft, dissemination, and exploitation of unreleased content.” Grande’s legal team outlines a pattern of illegal behavior in which hackers targeted the personal digital accounts of photographers and producers who worked closely with her and subsequently sold the data and content for “significant sums of money.”
	

	Grande is suing unnamed John Does to “uncover the identities of these currently unknown and unscrupulous individuals in order to hold them accountable for their invasive and reprehensible conduct.” The suit states that “it is imperative to Ms. Grande to ensure — on behalf of herself and others — that such conduct is deterred to the fullest extent possible.”


	The singer’s suit asserts that hundreds of leaks have occurred since she made her music debut in 2011. It claims that in 2019, hackers acquired the login for a Dropbox account that belonged to a photographer who had worked with Grande. The following year, the defendants hacked into the mobile device of a producer who had collaborated with Grande and accessed unreleased masters and demos and footage from recording sessions. In 2023 alone, hackers obtained access to 45 of her unreleased songs and leaked them.
	

	Additionally, the suit claims that in 2024, hackers created a Gmail account and domain name impersonating a photographer to get a digital technician to send unreleased photos that belonged to Grande.

	A representative for Grande did not immediately respond to Variety‘s request for additional comment.

schema.headline: Ariana Grande Sues Hackers for Leaking Unreleased Music and Footage

title: ‘Kill Jackie,’ Starring a Glamorous, Lethal Catherine Zeta-Jones, Acquired by Warner Bros. Discovery for HBO Max (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Warner Bros. Discovery has acquired revenge thriller “Kill Jackie,” starring Catherine Zeta-Jones, for HBO Max in Spain, Portugal, Sweden, Denmark,
body:
Warner Bros. Discovery has acquired revenge thriller “Kill Jackie,” starring Catherine Zeta-Jones, for HBO Max in Spain, Portugal, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland, Iceland, France and Belgium.

	The deal takes in two of HBO’s most established streaming markets, the Nordics and Spain, where SVOD services HBO Nordics and HBO España launched as far back as 2012 and 2016 with HBO Max set to pass Prime Video to become the second largest streamer in Spain by the end of 2026, according to Ampere Analysis. 
	

	Produced by Fremantle, which handles all international distribution outside the U.S., and Steel Spring Pictures, the eight-part series is scheduled to debut in 2026. “Kill Jackie” looks set to give Zeta-Jones, an Oscar, Bafta and Tony Award winner (“Chicago,” “Wednesday”), as she has recognised, a “multifaceted” role encompassing “empowerment, identity and redemption.”


	Zeta-Jones plays a drug dealer turned glamorous art dealer whose past suddenly caches up with her as she becomes the target of The Seven Demons, a hit squad of the world’s most terrifying assassins.

	When a tragic event makes her hell-bent for revenge, Jackie determines to take out the Demons one by one, unleashing her old killer instincts. “However, she soon realises her own demons are much more terrifying than the ruthless killers on her trail…and her buried secrets ultimately lead her much closer to home, with surprising consequences,” the synopsis runs.

	A buzz title at the London TV Screenings, “Kill Jackie” co-stars Daniel Ings (“The Knight of the Seven Kingdoms”) as Jackie’s foil, her distinctly sensitive-about-violence tax lawyer, who, according to reports, provides much of the humor in a consistently high-octane, twisting, comedic thriller.  
	

	Written by Tom Butterworth (“Gangs of London”) and Conor Keane, “Kill Jackie” is lead directed by Damon Thomas (“Killing Eve”), adapting “The Price You Pay” by Sunday Times best-selling author Nick Harkaway, writing as Aidan Truhen.

	Key cast also takes in another HBO alum, Sidse Babett Knudsen (“Prime Target,” “Borgen”),and  Óscar Jaenada , Hattie Hook, Darci Shaw, Raff Law , Enzo Cilenti, Christine Adams, Julian Rhind-Tutt, Karlis Arnolds Avots, Set Sjöstrand, Tadashi Ito, Sebastian Armesto, Julian Barratt, Gavin Spokes , Jonathan Cake, Bamshad Abedi-Amin and  Bill Paterson.

	“HBO Max has an outstanding track record of partnering on the very best projects, making it the perfect home for ‘Kill Jackie,’ said Jamie Lynn, EVP co-production & distribution EMEA. “As the platform continues to grow across Europe, we couldn’t be more delighted to embark on this adventure together. With its relentless pace, thrilling action and unforgettable central performance, we know ‘Kill Jackie’ is in the very best of hands.“

	“I loved Nick’s gonzo thriller of a book,” Butterworth has said. “Our ambition is to twist and expand his world into something equally funny, dark, crazed and unique. Or die trying.”

	“Kill Jackie” is a “sly character study that asks what happens when you’re forced to act out your darkest impulses in order to survive. But at its heart, it’s a grounded, universal story about family: the kind we’re born with and the kind we choose,” Fremantle told Variety is the run-up to Mipcom. 

	“Kill Jackie” is produced in partnership with José Luis Escolar’s Deabru Kalea Filmeak which supervised production in and around Bilbao. So expect the propulsive thriller to make full use of Bilbao’s extraordinarily chic post-industrial cityscape, taking advantage of its Guggenheim Museum, belle époque and modern plate glass architecture, estuary-adjunct walkways and green countryside. 

	“Killing Jackie” is co-created by Conor Keane, Butterworth Peter Lawson (“John Wick”) and Thomas. Butterworth serves as both writer and showrunner. 

	Executive producers are Lawson and Jose Agustín Valdés for Steel Springs Pictures, Butterworth, Thomas, Zeta-Jones, Rebecca Dundon, Dante Di Loreto and Jeffrey Levine, with Nick Harkaway serving as executive consultant.
	

	With the WBD deal, a multi-territory sales to Prime Video and a recent AMC+ U.S. sale, “Kill Jackie” has closed the lion’s share of major territories in the world.

	Zeta-Jones is represented by UTA and Ziffren Brittenham LLP. Butterworth is represented by Curtis Brown. Daniel Ings is represented by United Agents, WME, TFC Management, ColorCreative, Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern and CLD Communications.

title: San Sebastian Competition Title ‘In My Father’s Room’ Boarded by Bitter’s End for Sales (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
San Sebastian Film Festival competition title “In My Father’s Room” has been added to Bitters End‘s fall sales slate. 

	The film marks the feature
body:
San Sebastian Film Festival competition title “In My Father’s Room” has been added to Bitters End‘s fall sales slate. 

	The film marks the feature directorial debut of best-selling novelist Maha Harada.

	Known in Japan under the title “Muyou no Hito,” the drama is adapted from Harada’s own short story “An Unnecessary Man.” The cast includes Aoi Yu (“Wife of a Spy”), Ogata Issey (“Onoda,” “Silence,” “Yi Yi”), Nagayama Eita (“Monster”) and Watanabe Eri (“Shall We Dance?”). Kitagawa Yoshio, whose credits include “Evil Doesn’t Exist” and “Lost Land,” serves as cinematographer.
	

	The story follows Satomi, an employee at an art museum, after an envelope arrives bearing an unfamiliar key. It unlocks a room left behind by her father, dead a month earlier and alone at the time. Tracing what he did in his last days, Satomi uncovers a figure society had largely written off, one who nonetheless took quiet comfort in language, in tea ceremony and in small, overlooked beauty, and she comes to recognize the grace in how he lived.


	The project marks a screen debut for Harada, one of Japan’s most widely read authors, with more than 10 million copies of her books sold since she began publishing in 2006. Harada trained in Japanese literature and art history, then spent time at a trading firm and at museums, among them New York’s Museum of Modern Art, before shifting into freelance curatorial and cultural writing work. Her art-themed novels include “Canvas of Paradise” and “Guernica Cover-Up.”

	Bitters End will handle both the film’s international sales and its local release, which is scheduled for January 2027 in Japan.
	

	The distributor has spent more than 30 years bringing international auteur cinema to Japanese audiences, including work by Hamaguchi Ryusuke, Bong Joon Ho, the Dardenne brothers, Jia Zhangke, Roy Anderson and Gianfranco Rosi. Recent releases handled by the company include “Below the Clouds,” “Young Mothers,” “Sex/Love/Dreams,” “Anora” and “The Odyssey.” On the production front, its credits as a producer include the Oscar-winning “Drive My Car,” “Two Seasons, Two Strangers,” which took the Golden Leopard at Locarno, Cannes prizewinner “All of a Sudden” and “All the Lovers in the Night,” an Un Certain Regard selection at Cannes.

title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ First Reactions: Tom Holland Has ‘Never Been Better’ in a Sequel That Ditches ‘Multiverse Tedium’ and Delivers a ‘Grounded Spider-Man Tale’
description: “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” has finally been unveiled to members of the film press, who are calling Tom Holland‘s fourth standalone movie “a grounde
body:
“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” has finally been unveiled to members of the film press, who are calling Tom Holland‘s fourth standalone movie “a grounded Spider-Man tale” that is “thrilling, heartfelt and confidently character driven.”

	Fandango correspondent Erik Davis shared a glowing review on X, writing that director Destin Daniel Cretton’s sequel “feels deeper, more thoughtful and more mature than the previous trilogy.”


	“That maturity extends beyond the story to the action, with Cretton crafting some of my favorite Spider-Man fight sequences of the Holland era,” he added. “Part detective story, part psychological thriller, part buddy comedy (the Spider-Man/Punisher banter is so much fun), it stretches in exciting new directions before becoming a genuine love letter to the fans. When you see it, you’ll get it.”
	

	Critic Wendy Lee Szany wrote on X that she has “no notes” for “Brand New Day,” which delivered “top-tier action” and a few “tearjerker” moments. 

	TV host and entertainment journalist Brandon Pope echoed the praise. He wrote in his X review, “‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day‘ may be the most Marvel Marvel movie I’ve ever marveled. Destin Daniel Cretton honors beloved Spider-Man media — especially Raimi — to create something soulful + thrilling. Hulk, Punisher deliver. Big reveal lives up. The best of the Tom Holland Spidey series.”

	Film critic Peter Howell likewise adored the Marvel sequel. He wrote on X that “Brand New Day” cut back on the “multiverse tedium to give us a grounded Spider-Man tale that’s back to the city roots of the comic book hero we knew and loved.”
	

	“Tom Holland finally nails the sarcasm, angst and love hassles of Spidey/Peter Parker as Stan Lee first envisioned the character,” Howell added. “The film negotiates the emotional landmines left by ‘Spider-Man: No Way Home’ five years ago while a seriously scary villain emerges in the person of a malevolent telepath. Solid support from Zendaya, Jacob Batalon, Jon Bernthal, Mark Ruffalo and ‘Stranger Things’ star Sadie Sink.”

	Nexus Point staffer Kevin Verma wrote on X, “‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ is exactly the refresher Marvel needed. Tom Holland has never been better and the Spidey-Punisher pairing is pure gold. Destin Daniel Cretton outdoes himself, but the script is the real superhero- thrilling, heartfelt and confidently character driven.”

	Holland returns as Peter Parker/Spider-Man in “Brand New Day,” which is set four years after the events of “Spider-Man: No Way Home.” That movie ended with Doctor Strange casting a spell in which Peter is erased from everyone’s memory, so now the web-slinger is fighting crime in New York City without the support of MJ (Zendaya) and Ned (Jacob Batalon). A new threat emerges in the form of Sadie Sink’s mysterious villain at the same time as Peter’s spider powers begin evolving beyond his control. The supporting cast includes Mark Ruffalo as Hulk and Jon Bernthal as Punisher.

	Expectations for “Brand New Day” are sky high after 2021’s “No Way Home” became a pop culture sensation with $1.9 billion at the worldwide box office. It was Holland’s second billion-dollar-grossing “Spider-Man” movie after 2019’s “Far From Home” earned $1.1 billion on the heels of “Avengers: Endgame.” While Marvel has had its ups (“Deadpool and Wolverine”) and downs (“Captain America: Brave New World”) in recent years, “Brand New Day” should get the MCU back on strong box office footing ahead of December’s “Avengers: Doomsday.”

	Holland played a greater role in the development of “Brand New Day” compared to his previous “Spider-Man” movies. He took deep dives on the internet to understand what exactly Spider-Man fans wanted to see in his latest outing as Marvel’s iconic web-slinger, then took these fan ideas directly to studio executives and the movie’s screenwriters.

	 “What’s been really fun about this most recent movie is designing the suit and being a part of that process and understanding what we wanted to try and achieve,” Holland told LADbible about having greater involvement in the movie’s development this time around.
	

	“I have been actively sifting through the internet and trying to best understand what it is that the fans want from a ‘Spider-Man’ movie, and that’s been my driving force in these pitch meetings,” he added. “I think the producers, at times were like, absolutely sick of me, but I think it’s really important, because we make these movies for [the fans].”

	“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” opens in theaters nationwide July 31. Check out more first reactions in the posts below.

#SpiderManBrandNewDay reminded me why the story of Spider-Man resonates w/ me so much. He's hope. But he's also painfully human so bring tissues 😭Also the Tom/Zendaya chemistry was rom-com levels. And we need more Punisher in everything. And Sadie Sink… just wow! Liza too! pic.twitter.com/68jgm3htfs— Lyra Hale 🇵🇷🏳️‍🌈✍🏼 (@MsLyraHale) July 28, 2026




Peter Parker is changing, and so is the 'Spider-Man' franchise. #SpiderManBrandNewDay is the most emotional, most mature and most atmospheric installment in the franchise. It'll meet your expectations in some places and defy them in others. pic.twitter.com/iA0XsLl9rL— Brian Davids (@PickYourBrian) July 28, 2026


Spider-Man: Brand New Day is a solid new entry for Marvel. The story and themes of loneliness, change, and friendship all hit incredibly hard. It’s a bit overstuffed with too much going on at points. Sadie Sink’s story is the most weighty and shocking. #SpiderManBrandNewDay pic.twitter.com/QO6EKTkgXC— Hunter Bolding (@HunterBVideo) July 28, 2026


Destin Daniel Cretton brings incredible energy to the #Spiderman franchise. #Brandnewday is action-packed from start to finish. That sound design is incredible. this might be Tom Holland’s best outing as Spiderman to date. It’s the Summer of Tom Holland, Zendaya + John Bernthal— Jazz Tangcay (@jazzt) July 28, 2026

title: CNN’s Kaitlan Collins Was ‘Not Surprised’ Trump Insulted Her in White House Correspondents’ Dinner Speech: ‘That Happens Pretty Regularly Inside the Oval Office’
description: CNN‘s Kaitlan Collins was “not surprised” that U.S. President Donald Trump insulted her during his speech at Friday night’s White House Corresponden
body:
CNN‘s Kaitlan Collins was “not surprised” that U.S. President Donald Trump insulted her during his speech at Friday night’s White House Correspondents’ Dinner. 

	During an appearance on “The Daily Show” on Monday, Collins — who serves as CNN’s chief White House correspondent — debriefed the event with Jon Stewart. 

	“In the room, I was not surprised when he insulted me. That happens pretty regularly inside the Oval Office. This is just a bigger venue where it was happening,” Collins said. “What was most surprising to me was — the room was filled with a lot of his staffers, his cabinet, his allies, Republicans in Congress — it was so quiet in the room during the president’s remarks.” 
	

	“Do you think it’s because of how much they respect him?” Stewart asked, to which Collins cheekily replied: “Who’s to say.” 


	Collins received an award for her coverage of Trump’s contentious meeting with Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky during the dinner, which was rescheduled from April after a gunman crashed through security at the original event. In his speech, the president said Collins “shouldn’t get the award” and that it was “fake,” and then went on a tangent about how she should smile more. Trump also compared Collins to trans advocate Dylan Mulvaney, mentioning the 2023 Bud Light controversy where conservative customers boycotted the beer brand after Mulvaney posted a social media ad featuring her face on a can. 

	“I thought Kaitlan had really made it big with a major new sponsorship, but then I informed her that it wasn’t her on the Bud Light can, it was Dylan Mulvaney,” Trump said in his speech. Mulvaney responded to Trump in a TikTok video on Sunday, saying she was “honored” to be compared to Collins and the president’s attack was perhaps the “greatest compliment of all.”
	

	As Collins said, Trump has a history of insulting her and deflecting her questions, which Stewart pointed out are often pretty straightforward. “That’s why I ask the questions the way I do, is because I want anyone to be able to listen to what I’m asking — whether that’s at a briefing or during a moment with the president — and think, you know, I want to know the answer to that, too, or that is a good question,” Collins said. “I don’t want it to only serve one audience or one political leaning, I want anyone — from my family in Alabama, to people in the White House, to people in Washington — to be able to hear that question and think, ‘What is the answer to that?'” 

	Collins also thanked her CNN colleague Wolf Blitzer, who presented the awards to journalists at the dinner, saying that “he’s called me every day since Friday.” She concluded that despite Trump’s speech, “It’s really not about me and I don’t want it to be about my reaction.”

	“I think if you let it become about that, then it becomes a back-and-forth between the two of us,” she said. “And instead, I think it’s more effective to remind people in those moments where he is insulting me or he is criticizing me, about the question I asked or the reporting I did that he was so angry about in this moment — and the fact that I got an award for it really bothered him, clearly.”

	Watch Collins’ full interview on “The Daily Show” below.

schema.headline: CNN’s Kaitlan Collins Was ‘Not Surprised’ Trump Insulted Her in White House Correspondents’ Dinner Speech: ‘That Happens Pretty Regularly Inside the Oval Office’

title: San Sebastián Lineup: Pablo Larraín, Mike Leigh, Benjamín Naishtat and More
description: Buzzy new projects from “Jacky,” “Spencer” and “Maria” director Pablo Larraín, and Benjamín Naishtat will be joined by Mike Leigh’s “Tender Loving C
body:
Buzzy new projects from “Jacky,” “Spencer” and “Maria” director Pablo Larraín, and Benjamín Naishtat will be joined by Mike Leigh’s “Tender Loving Care” in main competition at September’s San Sebastián Film Festival.  

	Also making the cut are new titles from Nicole Garcia – Marion Coillard starrer “7:40 ce matin-là/Milo,’ as well as Maha Harada’s “In My Father’s Room,” Hans Petter Moland’s “Growth  of the Soil” and Yeşim Ustaoğlu’s “What Remains.” Announced Tuesday, the new titles reflect San Sebastián’s hallmark mix of international name auteurs – often drawn from its key source markets of Latin America, France and the Nordics – and newer talent, a key focus for San Sebastián whose New Directors strand, set to be announced on Friday, is one of the most prestigious in Europe.
	

	A feature version of Larraín’s Netflix four-part horror miniseries produced by Fabula, “My Sad Dead” (“Mis muertos tristes”) adapts Argentinean writer Mariana Enriquez, who suggests that the true terror is not the supernatural itself, but the horrors that society hides. Top Argentine actors Mercedes Morán, Dolores Fonzi and Alejandra Flechner star.


	Leigh’s “Tender Loving Care” stars Marion Bailey, Paul Jesson, Kate O’Flynn, Alice Bailey Johnson in what the festival describes as his “insightful exploration of the modern world.”

	From the director of “Rojo,” a big hit at San Sebastián, Naishtat’s “Glaxo” is a tale of shattered friendship set in a small provincial town between the late 1950s and the 1980s and described as “about desire and revenge, set at a time when a whole country lost its innocence.”
	

	San Sebastián’s newly announced Golden Shell contenders join three Spanish features in main competition which were announced on July 17: Mikel Gurrea’s “Sants,” with “The Beloved” star Vicky Luengo, top comedian Berto Romero’s time-loop relationship comedy “Five Minutes More” and Roberto Bueso’s family dramedy “El mal padre.”

	The 74th edition of the San Sebastian Film Festival, the biggest film event in the Spanish-speaking world, runs Sept. 18-26 in the capital of Gipuzcoa, in Spain’s verdant and stunning Basque Country. 

	More to come.

	Newly Announced San Sebastián Main Competition Titles

	“Milo” (“7:40 ce matin-là,” Nicole Garcia, France)

	“What Remains” (“Artakalan,” Yeşim Ustaoğlu, Turkey/France/ /Luxembourg/Bulgaria)

	“Glaxo” (Benjamín Naishtat, Brazil/Argentina) Cast: Lali Espósito, Esteban Lamothe, and Marcelo Subiotto

	Produced by Brazil’s RT Features and Argentina’s Rei Pictures with a top Argentine cast of Espósito (“Permitidos,” “Sky Rojo”), Esteban Lamothe (“The Student”) and Marcelo Subiotto (“Puan”) and a tale which explores macro historical transformation via an intimate narrative, a winning combination in Rojo’s pre-junta portrayal of “moral apocalypse,” as Variety noted. 

	“Growth of the Soil” (“Markens Grode,” Hans Petter Moland, Norway/Denmark/Germany )

	“My Sad Dead” (“Mis muertos tristes,” Pablo Larraín, Argentina-Chile) Cast: Mercedes Morán, Dolores Fonzi, Carolina Álvarez

	A world premiere. Ema, who can see and hear the dead, receives an unexpected visit from her niece Julie, who shares the same unsettling gift. As family secrets and wounds, resurface the entire neighborhood senses presences and hear the distinctive sounds of their own dead. Written by Larráin and among co-scribes, Guillermo Calderón, co-writer of “Neriuda” “El Conde,” and adapting Mariana Enríquez. “Mariana’s writing is particularly visual, always brilliant, and always dangerous. It’s a casual, domestic horror that inspires,” says Larraín. 

	“In My Father’s Room” (“Muyou no hito,” Maha Harada, Japan)

	“Tender Loving Care” (Mike Leigh, U.K./U.S./Singapore) Cast: Marion Bailey, Paul Jesson, Kate O’Flynn, and Alice Bailey Johnson.
	

	The latest from Leigh, a Cannes Palme d’Or winner with “Secrets and Lies” and multiple Oscar nominee, set yo world premiere at Toronto, sold by Cornerstone with its split still under wraps save that it offers an “insightful exploration of the modern world.”

schema.headline: San Sebastián Lineup: Pablo Larraín, Mike Leigh, Benjamín Naishtat and More

title: Lee Chang-dong’s Venice and Toronto-Bound ‘Possible Love’ Sets Theatrical Release Dates Ahead of Netflix Bow
description: Lee Chang-dong‘s “Possible Love” will open in Korean theaters September 23, followed by select theatrical releases in Australia Oct. 22 and in the U
body:
Lee Chang-dong‘s “Possible Love” will open in Korean theaters September 23, followed by select theatrical releases in Australia Oct. 22 and in the U.S., Canada, U.K., Ireland and Japan Oct. 23, before streaming globally on Netflix starting November 6.

	The film’s world premiere will be at the Venice Film Festival and North American Premiere at the Toronto Film Festival. 

	“Possible Love” marks Lee’s first feature in eight years, following “Burning,” “Poetry” and “Secret Sunshine.” The film centers on two married couples whose lives intersect after a funeral: Mi-ok and her laid-off husband Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu), who live quietly with their young son Cheol, and Ye-ji, a filmmaker making a documentary about workers who lost their jobs, and her husband Sang-woo (Zo In-sung). When Mi-ok agrees to be filmed by Ye-ji, the two women grow close, while Mi-ok finds herself unsettled by an attraction to Sang-woo. As the two couples’ worlds overlap, cracks begin to surface in both marriages.
	

	The cast brings together Jeon Do-yeon (“Secret Sunshine”), Sul Kyung-gu (“Peppermint Candy”), Zo In-sung (“Escape From Mogadishu”) and Cho Yeo-jeong (“Parasite”) in what stands as one of the largest gatherings of top-tier Korean acting talent in a single film.


	Lee also co-wrote the screenplay with Oh Jung-mi. The film is produced by Pinehouse Film Co., Ltd., Anonymous Content, LLC and Nowfilm Co., Ltd, with South Korea as its country of origin.

	With festival berths at Venice and Toronto locked in ahead of its theatrical rollout, “Possible Love” positions itself as one of the more closely watched Korean auteur releases of the fall season before landing on Netflix worldwide.

schema.headline: Lee Chang-dong’s Venice and Toronto-Bound ‘Possible Love’ Sets Theatrical Release Dates Ahead of Netflix Bow

title: Zendaya Stuns ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Premiere in ‘Abstract’ Spider-Inspired Look: ‘It’s Like This Metamorphosis’
description: Zendaya stunned the red carpet at the “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” Los Angeles premiere in a black satin Ashi Studio corset with a sweeping architect
body:
Zendaya stunned the red carpet at the “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” Los Angeles premiere in a black satin Ashi Studio corset with a sweeping architectural train, putting an exclamation point on a press tour that the young star used as her personal runway.

	“It’s kind of an abstract way to present the spider,” Law Roach, Zendaya’s longtime stylist, told Variety of the look during the Monday night premiere. “You know, in our mind, it’s like this metamorphosis of this woman into this thing. And the jewelry is Boucheron.”
	

	While Roach said he “can’t pick a favorite” look from the tour, he shouted out the archival spiderweb dress from John Galliano’s 1997 “Circus” collection that Zendaya rocked in June at the London premiere of the Marvel sequel.

	When asked about his plans for the “Dune: Part Three” press tour, Roach was tight-lipped on details, but shared, “’Dune’ is a bit away, but it’s gonna be great. I’m excited.”

	Zendaya made headlines last month by skipping the couture and wearing a vintage Spider-Man T-shirt to a “Brand New Day” fan event in Paris. Roach scooped up the shirt on eBay for just $34.99. After the look when live, Roach posted the listing for the tee on his Instagram Story with the caption, “Style doesn’t always have to cost a fortune.”

	Zendaya stars alongside her husband, Tom Holland, in “Brand New Day,” which sees Peter Parker navigate a world in which his friends and family have forgotten him. Other cast members include Mark Ruffalo, Jon Bernthal, Jacob Batalon, Sadie Sink, Liza Colón-Zayas and Tramell Tillman. Destin Daniel Cretton serves as director.
	

	“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” hits theaters on July 31.

schema.headline: Zendaya Stuns ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Premiere in ‘Abstract’ Spider-Inspired Look: ‘It’s Like This Metamorphosis’

title: Azealia Banks' Ex-Manager Slams Restraining Order as 'Desperate' Act After His Recent Court Win
body:
Update
  
    
            07:16 PM PT -- Jeff's lawyer, Michael E. Weinsten, tells TMZ, "This purported filing by Ms Banks is just the latest desperate ... act from someone who has already been found liable in a court of law for defaming my client over many years, threatening this family, interfering with his business and other outrageous conduct."
      
    
            Jeff sued Azealia in 2020 for alleged defamation, stalking, invasion of privacy and civil extortion. She denied the claims. The singer filed a countersuit, but the claims were dismissed. Jeff's lawsuit against Azealia remains ongoing.
      
    
            Jeff's lawyer said they recently completed a trial on the issue of damages where they put forth evidence of the alleged damage caused by "Ms. Banks and her antics."
      
    
            Michael tells TMZ, "We are expecting a ruling in the coming months and look forward to the court holding Ms. Banks fully accountable for her actions." He said the singer had the chance to raise her "alleged grievances" in the lawsuit, "but all of her claims were dismissed ... with prejudice."
      
    
            Azealia Banks just filed for a temporary restraining order against her ex-manager, claiming he psychologically and emotionally abused her for over a decade.
      
    
            According to Monday’s filing, obtained by TMZ, AB says she’s been abused by Jeff Kwatinetz since 2014, when he allegedly got her to sign up for a life insurance policy when she was intoxicated.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Banks claims ... “He gave me expensive red wine and put the policy in front of me when I was drunk and we were cozied up.”
      

            Azealia alleges the policy wasn’t reviewed by a lawyer -- and she wasn’t even sure if her attorney knew about it. She claims JK won’t tell her if the policy is still active or who benefits from it.
      
    
            When describing her relationship with Jeff in the new filing, Azealia checked the box that said “we are dating or used to date,” alleging in her declaration that they had an “intimate and very close relationship” and accusing him of mixing their personal relationship with his control over her career.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The rapper also accused Kwatinetz of hiring a private security firm to “locate and profile” her, alleging they were “mapping” her home from the air.
      
    
            She claims that during this time, she once came home to a “wide-open window” and would see “random unmarked cars” near her homes when she would move from state to state. She also alleged that he’d falsely accused her of trying to rob his house.
      
    
            In the filing, Azealia claims the most recent abuse went down in November, accusing Kwatinetz of coercive control, financial exploitation, blackmail and disturbing her peace ... while also alleging that he hasn’t spoken to her directly in about 10 years.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            She alleges he demanded she extend her recording contract and make more music to line his pockets … while she says he was falsely telling the court that she refused to be deposed.
      
    
            In case you weren’t aware ... Jeff first sued Azealia back in 2020 for alleged extortion. Jeff moved for dismissal, but then filed another complaint in 2021 alleging stalking, defamation, and civil extortion. She was ultimately found liable.
      
    
            Not only is the artist asking for a stay-away and no-contact order, she’s also asking for protection for her mom, sister, niece and nephew ... claiming that he may try to go through them to get to her.
      
    
            Azealia’s also asking that he disclose and cancel the alleged life insurance policy, doesn’t hire anyone to monitor her and allow her to appear remotely for any hearings.
      
    
            To be clear, Azealia isn’t alleging physical abuse in her filing, but instead that she suffered psychological and emotional abuse at the hands of Kwatinetz.
      
    
            We’ve reached out to Jeff for comment ... so far no word back.

schema.headline: Azealia Banks' Ex-Manager Slams Restraining Order as 'Desperate' Act After His Recent Court Win
